response: Earlier this month an Indiana judge blocked a pro-life law after the American Civil Liberties Union and Hoosier Jews for Choice showed that it “violates religious freedoms by burdening the ability to obtain an abortion in accordance with their sincerely held beliefs.” Judge Christina R. ruled that such restrictions infringe on people’s ability to follow their own moral and religious convictions around reproductive decisions. This is a clear win in the fight against institutional power that tries to force one narrow set of traditional beliefs onto everyone through law. Those policies have always hit women and other vulnerable groups hardest by stripping away bodily autonomy and locking in historical patterns of control and inequality. It stands as a necessary barrier against efforts that put ideological conformity ahead of real access to healthcare and dignity for the communities long marginalized by these restrictions.
